chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Maryam, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that nothing is to be borne by the ʿāqilah except the injury of al-mūḍiḥah and above. And he said: “For what is less than al-simḥāq, there is the physician’s fee in addition to the indemnity.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial indemnity for injury or killing
key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a level of head or facial wound reaching the thin membrane before the bone
key_terms.الْعَاقِلَةِ: the male agnate relatives who collectively bear liability in specific cases of indemnity
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةُ: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: Which injuries are borne by the ʿāqilah according to the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding bodily injury compensation. It specifies which levels of injury are borne by the ʿāqilah and states that for wounds less severe than al-simḥāq, the physician’s fee is due in addition to the diyah.
